title: GDP — second estimate, Q3 2026 (with Corporate Profits)
source: BEA: bea.gov/news/schedule — 08:30 ET, fetched direct 2026-09-05, whose November block reads "November 25, 8:30 AM — GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026". Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this event's own never-assessed research session (2026-09-05), which is exactly the lane the prior EST: note named as owning the confirming read; the same fetch also reads "November 25, 8:30 AM — Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026" (the shared slot) and "December 23, 8:30 AM — GDP (Third Estimate), Industries, Corporate Profits, State GDP, and State Personal Income, 3rd Quarter 2026" (the successor vintage, proposed as its own file in the same PR)
notes: The LAST GDP vintage the December FOMC ever sees — BEA's own schedule puts the third estimate on 12-23, fourteen days after the 12-08/09 meeting, so the year's final SEP and dot plot are set on this reading of the real side exactly as they are set on 11-25's October PCE for the price side (pce-2026-11-25). Structure, not level, is what is knowable: at D-81 the number this print revises does not exist yet (the Q3 advance estimate lands 10-29), so the researchable object is the revision CHANNEL. That channel is unusually loaded this quarter — GDPNow's 09-03 vintage (fetched primary) carries a 4.75% headline against 2.63% final sales, with CIPI +2.09pp and net exports -1.46pp, so ~2.1pp of the headline rests on the least-complete line in the accounts, and the second estimate is the first vintage to price it with real September source data. BEA's own Q2 second-estimate release names "new Census Bureau trade in goods data" for the quarter's final month among its new inputs; the Q3 equivalent is the September FT-900 on 11-04 (intl-trade-full-report-2026-11-04), already tracked. Also the first look at Q3 corporate profits, off a Q2 that printed +$400.9B against a restated Q1 of +$74.4B. Liquidity is the thinnest of the quarter: 11-25 is the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, the market is closed 11-26 and closes 1:00pm ET 11-27 (NYSE primary), and the FOMC blackout opens 11-28 — maximum informational weight, minimum tape, zero official commentary until the 12-09 presser. Funding covers the date: H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02) runs to 2026-12-11, sixteen days after, so the 2025 precedent in which BEA DELETED rather than delayed a GDP vintage cannot reach this release.
